definition.name: schur_weyl_duality
definition.definition: Schur-Weyl duality decomposes (C^d)^{tensor n} into irreducible representations of both the symmetric group S_n and the unitary group U(d). The decomposition is: (C^d)^{tensor n} = bigoplus_{lambda |- n, ell(lambda) <= d} Sp_lambda tensor V_lambda^d, where lambda ranges over partitions of n with at most d parts, Sp_lambda is the Specht module (irrep of S_n with dimension dim(lambda)), and V_lambda^d is the Weyl module (irrep of U(d)). The Schur transform is the unitary implementing this change of basis, mapping the computational basis to the Schur basis with registers (Y, P, Q) for the Young diagram label, permutation (Specht), and unitary group (Weyl) degrees of freedom respectively.
